proposed.explanation: Overspecifies the requirement; specifications typically allow equivalent products unless specific performance requires a particular brand. Attributes budget control to the architect; document detail supports accurate bidding, but does not guarantee bids will fall within budget. Confuses document adequacy with on-site supervision; detailed documents reduce, rather than eliminate, the need for on-site verification. The architect must prepare drawings and specifications that are sufficiently detailed for competitive bidding and construction execution. These documents must comply with all applicable laws, codes, and regulations, allowing contractors to bid accurately without constant clarification. Documents must provide enough detail for accurate bidding and code-compliant execution; excessive brand specification is neither required nor typical practice.
